newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The African National Congress offered to elevate Inkatha Freedom Party leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi in central government to a still undefined position, in exchange for his giving up the chairmanship of the KwaZulu-Natal house of traditional leaders.
- Police and the South African Revenue Service have said they intend investigating allegations that the KWV wine cooperative sold fake Champagne in the early 1990s.

- South Africa's drive to build foreign exchange reserves will shift up a gear next week when Finance Minister Trevor Manuel and his team go to New York for a roadshow aimed at launching a 20-year Yankee bond issue of about $500 million.

- Zimbabwe's private mning companies say the state's monopoly over the annual export of base minerals worth about two billion rand results in a bureaucracy which strangles orders and imposes unnecessary costs.
- El Nino is back after a two-year absence, portending drought, reduced crops, higher import bills and lower gross domestic product across much of southern Africa.

- Saflife's attributable income surged 600 percent to 157 million rand in the year to March, after the group's disposal of a 60.6 percent holding in Global Capital to subsidiary Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd generated non-recurring profit of 122 million rand.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Platinum and palladium soared on Friday after a serious shortage on international spot markets drove prices above $500 an ounce for platinum at one point, but analysts said the highs were unlikely to last.

- The rate on three-month trasury bills dropped nearly 20 basis points at Friday's weekly auction to 15.46 percent from 15.64 percent, a sign of expectation that long-term interest rates would soon fall.

- Paper and pulp producer Sappi has signed a strategic joint venture with Norwegian chemicals firm Borregaard, a division of the Orkla ASA group, for the establishment of a 100 million rand, 55,000 tonne per year lignosulphate plant on the KwaZulu-Natal south coast.
- South Africa's third cellular licence will be issued before the end of the year, Nape Maepa, chairman of the South African Telecommunications Regulatory Authority said.
- Coca-Cola on Friday announced a $45 million investment to double its business in Mozambique over the next four years.
SAKE-BEELD
- The pension fund for workers in the public service has assets of 126 billion rand, with 26 percent of that invested in the share market.
- South Africa is one of 10 countries which have not yet implemented the trade protocol of the 12-nation South African Development Community, which was signed last year.

- South Afirca, biggest producer of platinum group metals for the world market, does not have stockpiles which could reduce the current shortages in platinum or palladium, according to Barry Davidson, managing director of Anglo American Platinum Corp.
- Teachers and civil servants are threatening a countrywide strike in Swaziland after salary negotiations deadlocked.
THE CITIZEN
- A new political party could be in the offing by the end of the year, after the National Consultative Forum of Bantu Holomisa and the New Movement Process of Roelf Meyer formed a joint committee.

- Nine South Africans were trapped by heavy artillery fire in a hotel in the Congolese capital Brazzaville, and Foreign Affairs Ministry officials were trying to include them in a French evacuation operation.
- A draft sports bill, which if ratified will give the government effective control of all sport, was slammed as unconstitutional by National Sports Council president Mluleki George.
